across six categories and three currencies (65 EUR, 36 USD, 19 GBP). All figures

97.2% of envelope, so the quarter closes broadly on plan in aggregate. That
headline is misleading, though: the aggregate is the net of two categories
running well over budget and four running comfortably under, and monthly spend
rose in both month-over-month comparisons.

EUR 12,137.98 (27.6% of the quarter), followed by software at EUR 9,702.03
(22.0%), training at EUR 8,992.94 (20.4%) and hardware at EUR 8,874.09 (20.2%).
Meals (EUR 2,541.26, 5.8%) and office (EUR 1,775.45, 4.0%) are small by
comparison. The average transaction was EUR 366.86.

story: eight separate dock purchases totalling EUR 5,043.25, or 56.8% of the
category, plus a single EUR 1,312.26 cable order that is the largest transaction
of the quarter. Travel is dominated by ground transport rather than flights —
taxis (EUR 3,720.13 over six rides) and car rentals (EUR 3,587.62 over five)
together account for 60.2% of travel spend, against EUR 2,235.59 of flights.
Software is spread across recurring commitments (seven SaaS subscriptions at
EUR 2,631.08 and seven license renewals at EUR 3,383.33) plus plugins and API
credits.

Roughly half the quarter's spend — 50.3% — was invoiced in USD or GBP, so these
totals carry meaningful FX exposure.

## Key figures

| Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Total Q2 spend | EUR 44,023.75 |
| Average transaction | EUR 366.86 |
| Largest transaction | EUR 1,312.26 (cables, hardware, 23 May, GBP 1,121.59) |
| May vs April | +9.8% |
| June vs May | +10.0% |
| Travel share | 27.6% |

Monthly spend rose from EUR 13,316.21 in April to EUR 14,623.21 in May and
EUR 16,084.33 in June — an accelerating base, not a one-off spike.

| Category | Total (EUR) | Budget (EUR) | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| travel | 12,137.98 | 10,300.00 | over |
| software | 9,702.03 | 8,200.00 | over |
| training | 8,992.94 | 10,800.00 | under |
| hardware | 8,874.09 | 10,700.00 | under |
| meals | 2,541.26 | 3,100.00 | under |
| office | 1,775.45 | 2,200.00 | under |

+10.0%. Two consecutive months at that rate means June alone annualises to a
quarter of EUR 48,252.99 — about 106.5% of the current EUR 45,300.00 envelope.

single most important thing to get ahead of before Q3 budgets are set.

58.2% of the entire quarter's travel spend in one month, across 10 transactions.

three taxi rides of EUR 995.00, EUR 1,278.28 and EUR 629.37. Taxis at that level
are usually a policy failure, not a market price. Recommend a pre-approval
threshold for ground transport above roughly EUR 500 and a push toward rail,

fragmentation here that a consolidation pass (same-vendor renewals, unused
seats, overlapping tools) is the most likely source of a quick saving.

EUR 5,043.25 were spread across the quarter at prices ranging from EUR 243.02 to

teams are buying independently at retail rather than through a single
procurement. Bulk purchasing, or at minimum confirming these units are actually
deployed, is worth a day of someone's time.

GBP. A move in either rate flows straight into reported spend, so some of the
10% monthly growth and part of the travel overrun may be rate rather than
volume. Worth separating volume from FX effect before concluding how much of the
trend is real.

**Underuses are consistent, not corrective.** Training (83.3%), hardware (82.9%),
meals (82.0%) and office (80.7%) all finished in a narrow band just above 80%.
That reads as budgets set with a standard cushion rather than deliberate
restraint, and it is what allowed the two overruns to hide inside an
on-plan-looking total. If Q3 budgets are rebased, these four are the place to
look for the headroom.

headline is misleading, though: the aggregate is the net of two categories
running well over budget and four running comfortably under, and monthly spend
rose in both month-over-month comparisons.

Spend is concentrated in four roughly equal blocks. Travel is the largest at
EUR 12,137.98 (27.6% of the quarter), followed by software at EUR 9,702.03
(22.0%), training at EUR 8,992.94 (20.4%) and hardware at EUR 8,874.09 (20.2%).
Meals (EUR 2,541.26, 5.8%) and office (EUR 1,775.45, 4.0%) are small by
comparison. The average transaction was EUR 366.86.

story: eight separate dock purchases totalling EUR 5,043.25, or 56.8% of the
category, plus a single EUR 1,312.26 cable order that is the largest transaction
of the quarter. Travel is dominated by ground transport rather than flights —
taxis (EUR 3,720.13 over six rides) and car rentals (EUR 3,587.62 over five)
together account for 60.2% of travel spend, against EUR 2,235.59 of flights.
Software is spread across recurring commitments (seven SaaS subscriptions at
EUR 2,631.08 and seven license renewals at EUR 3,383.33) plus plugins and API
credits.

totals carry meaningful FX exposure.
